mcqs.question: Which features does CG84 tell you to ask about when assessing dehydration and shock?

options.A: Unwell appearance, altered responsiveness, low urine output, pale or mottled skin, and cold extremities
options.B: Only the number of loose stools
options.C: Blood pressure in every infant before any history
options.E: Skin turgor is the only permitted sign

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Unwell appearance, altered responsiveness, low urine output, pale or mottled skin, and cold extremities
mcqs.explanation: CG84 lists those clinical features for remote or face-to-face assessment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: appears unwell has altered responsiveness, for example is irritable or lethargic has decreased urine output has pale or mottled skin has cold extremities

mcqs.question: How does CG84 describe deficit replacement with low-osmolarity ORS?

options.D: No oral fluid if the child is dehydrated

mcqs.explanation: CG84 says give 50 ml/kg for fluid deficit replacement over 4 hours as well as maintenance fluid.

sourceRefs.excerpt: give 50 ml/kg for fluid deficit replacement over 4 hours as well as maintenance fluid

mcqs.question: What osmolarity does CG84 specify for the oral rehydration solution?
mcqs.explanation: CG84 specifies a low-osmolarity solution of 240–250 mOsm/L.

sourceRefs.excerpt: solution (240–250 mOsm/l) for oral rehydration therapy

mcqs.question: When does CG84 say to measure venous acid–base status and chloride?

options.A: If shock is suspected or confirmed
options.B: In every child with one vomit
options.E: Only if the child is over 12 years

mcqs.correctAnswerText: If shock is suspected or confirmed
mcqs.explanation: CG84 recommends that blood test if shock is suspected or confirmed.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Measure venous blood acid–base status and chloride concentration if shock is suspected or confirmed.

mcqs.question: Which two states does CG84 section 1.2 tell clinicians to assess together?
mcqs.explanation: The section is titled assessing dehydration and shock.
